title: Unencrypted GPS Transmission
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) without encryption, exposing sensitive location data.
assumptions: Device capabilities and network security posture are assumed sufficient to transmit raw GPS data.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: Backend (P1) receives and stores the unencrypted GPS coordinates from the child device (EE2), creating a data flow where sensitive location data is processed and potentially stored.
assumptions: Backend system is assumed to have appropriate security controls to prevent unauthorized access or leakage.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) writes location pings to the Location History Store (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system transfers personal data (location data) to a third-party data store, which may be considered a third-party entity or a data processing function. This is an explicit disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: The location data is considered personal data under the LINDDUN framework.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives and stores location pings from the backend process (P1). This represents a data disclosure where the store acts as a data processing function or a data repository for personal data, transferring the data from the source process.
assumptions: The location data is considered personal data under the LINDDUN framework.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) forwards new location pings to the Geofencing Engine (P2). This constitutes a data disclosure as P1 transfers personal location data to a third-party process (P2) for processing.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives and processes location pings from P1. This is a data disclosure as P2 processes personal location data from a third-party process (P1).

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: A malicious actor could potentially access the Family Account Store (DS2) and extract the configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) intended for the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). This data is sensitive personal information (PII) that should not be exposed to an external process without explicit authorization.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine is not currently configured with any authentication or access control mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific zone definitions contain PII or if the store is publicly accessible.

title: Unauthorized Data Exfiltration
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) could potentially be compromised or misconfigured to exfiltrate the zone definitions from the Family Account Store (DS2) to an unauthorized external entity or another process.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine has no known security controls or audit logs in place.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the engine is currently running or if it has been compromised.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: An external entity (EE1) may attempt to access or manipulate the geofencing data flow (P2) without proper authorization, potentially leading to unauthorized location data exposure.
assumptions: The system allows external entities to interact with the process without explicit permission checks.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific threat type 'L' (Unauthorized Access) is the most appropriate classification for this interaction type, as the context suggests a push notification mechanism. However, given the potential for external entities to access the flow, this is a plausible threat.

title: Data Exfiltration via Geofencing Engine
description: An external entity (EE1) may attempt to exfiltrate or manipulate the geofencing data flow (P2) by sending unauthorized data or commands, potentially leading to data loss or manipulation.
assumptions: The system allows external entities to interact with the process without explicit permission checks.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific threat type 'D' (Data Exfiltration) is the most appropriate classification for this interaction type, as the context suggests a push notification mechanism. However, given the potential for external entities to manipulate the flow, this is a plausible threat.

title: Data Leakage
description: Parent (ExternalEntity) registers an account, creating a child profile. The child's sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school) is stored in the Mobile App Backend (Process). This flow represents a direct data flow from an external entity to a process, where sensitive personal information is being collected and stored.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives the parent's account registration and the child's sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school). This process is storing and potentially exposing this data to unauthorized parties.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) transfers account, child profile, and geofence zone data to the Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process is transferring personal data across a boundary to a data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The data store (DS2) receives data from the backend process (P1) and stores it. This is a data disclosure as the store is receiving personal data across a boundary.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Access

title: Data Disclosure

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History

title: Data Exfiltration Risk

assumptions: Assumption: The backend process does not implement adequate data protection or encryption for the retrieved location history.

title: Unauthorized Location Sharing
description: Parent (EE1) initiates a data flow to a Process (P1) to share location data with a secondary guardian. This action is triggered by the parent's intent to invite a relative, creating a privacy risk where location data is exposed to an unauthorized third party.
assumptions: The parent has the authority to share location data with a secondary guardian.

title: Location Data Exposure
description: The data flow from the Parent (EE1) to the Mobile App Backend (P1) transmits location data. This data-centric threat arises at the data flow itself, where the transmission of location information to a third-party process (the guardian) could be intercepted, logged, or used to identify the parties involved.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes and transmits the location data to the external entity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Secondary Guardian
description: Process P1 grants access to ExternalEntity EE3, which is an external system. This interaction is valid under the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity), but the granularity of the threat type (L) is appropriate for a high-severity privacy risk where the external entity is a secondary guardian.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is an external system that has access to the child's live location data.

title: Data Leakage to External Entity
description: ExternalEntity EE3 is sharing the child's live location data with Process P1. This is a valid interaction (ExternalEntity->Process) and constitutes a data leakage (D) threat type.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is sharing live location data with the backend process.

title: Data Leakage
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are shared with an external advertising/analytics partner, potentially exposing sensitive user data.
assumptions: The partner has access to the raw or aggregated data flows.

title: Data Leakage
description: The advertising/analytics partner may access or misuse the shared aggregated usage and engagement analytics.
assumptions: The partner has access to the data.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity) sends a manual check-in / SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process). This message is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Mobile App Backend (Process) receives and stores a manual check-in / SOS message with the Child's current location. This data is attributed to the user (EE2) and constitutes non-repudiable data evidence of their location.
